candidate.name: loop_breaker
candidate.hypothesis: A deterministic repetition-triggered recovery reminder injected into the request only when the trailing action/observation sequence repeats (two identical consecutive actions or a genuine period-2/period-3 cycle) will break non-progressing loops, lifting pass rate above the 0.22 identity-incumbent baseline; non-repetitive trajectories are left byte-identical.
candidate.changes: In agents/loop_breaker.py (single focused mechanism, transform_request only; transform_response is identity): statelessly reconstruct the last 12 (action, observation) pairs from request messages (action from assistant tool_calls JSON with name fallback; observation from the following tool/user message with the trailing AVAILABLE ACTIONS list stripped before comparison). On trigger, append a deterministic ~400-char reminder to the last message's content: repeated action/cycle and count, the goal text extracted verbatim from the first user message, and generic directives (choose a different offered action; never repeat the same action twice in a row; try unvisited locations/unexplored containers; verify the object name and required state against the goal). No trigger or malformed input returns the original request unchanged; no new messages, no tools change, no cross-episode state, stdlib imports only.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Reminder adds ~60-120 tokens only on triggered calls (measured 349/2010 calls in the baseline evidence; 0/41 calls in passing episodes). Expected to cut failed-episode token average (327K) and 50-turn exhaustion by breaking loops; passing episodes unchanged. Pass rate predicted 0.22 -> 0.28-0.32.

candidate.name: state_precondition_nudge
candidate.hypothesis: Appending a goal-derived required-state precondition reminder whenever the history contains no offered transform action (clean/heat/cool) on the goal object will convert a substantial share of state-precondition failures into passes, lifting the pass rate above the 0.32 incumbent, while non-state-goal episodes stay byte-identical to loop_breaker.
candidate.changes: In agents/state_precondition_nudge.py (one new mechanism layered on a byte-for-byte copy of loop_breaker's repetition reminder; transform_request only, transform_response identity): extract the goal text as before, parse it with two regexes -- '<clean|heat|cool> some <object> [and put it in/on <dest>]' and 'put a <clean|hot|cool> <object> in/on <dest>' (hot maps to verb heat), tolerant of articles, multi-word phrases and trailing numeric indices. Stateless suppression: if any earlier assistant action was present in the preceding AVAILABLE ACTIONS list AND starts with the parsed verb AND contains the object token, the request is returned unchanged (off-list attempts are silent no-ops in this environment and do NOT suppress). Otherwise append a deterministic ~300-char reminder (after any loop reminder) naming the object, required state and destination, stating that the transform action is offered only while holding the object at the appliance, that actions outside the offered list have no effect, and the sequence find/take -> carry -> offered transform -> deliver. Non-state or unparsable goals, and any malformed input, return the original request unchanged. Stdlib json/re only, no new calls, no cross-episode state.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Reminder adds ~80 tokens only on calls before the goal-object transform is actually performed (fires roughly on turns 1..k of the ~24 state-goal episodes, ~50 calls each at most); pass episodes are otherwise unchanged. Expect 2-5 of the state-goal failures to flip from 50-turn/~410K-token exhaustion to ~15-25 turns/~80-120K (cf. passing counterexample at 25 turns/112K), lowering mean failed-episode tokens a few percent. Pass rate predicted 0.32 -> 0.38-0.44.

candidate.name: light_goal_hold_nudge
candidate.hypothesis: When the goal asks to look at or examine an object under/with a lamp-like device, the history already shows a chosen non-take action on that device, and no offered take of the goal object has been chosen, appending a deterministic hold reminder (the task completes only while the object is in hand and the device is on) will convert a substantial share of 50-turn lamp-device exhaustion failures into passes, while every other episode stays byte-identical to state_precondition_nudge.
candidate.changes: In agents/light_goal_hold_nudge.py (byte-for-byte copy of state_precondition_nudge plus ONE new stateless layer; transform_response stays identity; layers applied repetition -> state -> light): parse the casefolded goal with a third regex '^(look at|examine) [the|a|an] <object> (under|with) [the] <device containing lamp|light>'; the object token goes through the existing trailing-index-stripping helper and the device is kept as captured. Trigger: at least one earlier assistant action (existing _extract_action) whose normalized text contains the device as a whole word and does not start with 'take' (e.g. a chosen 'use desklamp 1' or 'examine desklamp 1'). Suppression mirroring _transform_already_chosen: if an earlier assistant action starting with 'take' and containing the object token was itself present in its preceding AVAILABLE ACTIONS list (existing _offered_before), return the request unchanged. Otherwise append '\n\n' plus a deterministic ~307-320 char reminder built only from the parsed object and device: to look at the object under the device the task completes only while HOLDING the object and the device is on, switching the device on or off again does not finish it, find the object, if 'take' is not offered empty your hands first, take the object, then use the device while still holding it. Malformed input, a non-lamp goal, or no matching device action returns the original request. No new imports, calls, or cross-episode state.
candidate.expected_efficiency: The layer fires only on lamp-goal episodes from the first chosen non-take device action until an offered take of the goal object is chosen. Verified replay over the 50 recorded incumbent requests: 44 episodes byte-identical; the 5 lamp-goal failures get the reminder on 38-48 calls each (219 calls, roughly +90 tokens per call, about +20K tokens overall); 1 passing lamp-goal episode fires on 3 calls where the reminder restates the plan the agent already follows (take the object), so residual risk is limited to that episode's 3 prompts. Expect 3-5 of the 5 failures to flip from 50-turn / ~220-340K-token exhaustion to ~12-25 turns, lifting the pass rate from 0.58 toward 0.62-0.68; mean tokens roughly flat (per-call overhead on remaining failures offset by large savings on flipped episodes).

candidate.name: stuck_search_redirect
candidate.hypothesis: For put-family goals, when the goal object has never been successfully picked up and the trailing actions stall (one action repeats, or a take/put/clean/heat/cool/use action produced an observation without its success phrase) while offered go-to/open actions remain unchosen, appending a stateless redirect naming the goal object and the still-unvisited offered actions will convert stuck 50-turn put-family failures into passes, lifting the pass rate above the 0.64 incumbent; episodes with no such signature stay byte-identical to light_goal_hold_nudge.
candidate.changes: In agents/stuck_search_redirect.py (byte-for-byte copy of light_goal_hold_nudge plus ONE new stateless layer applied after repetition -> state -> light; transform_response stays identity): parse the goal text with plain-put regexes 'put [some|a|an|the|two] <object> in/on <dest>' and 'find <word> <object> and put them in/on <dest>', reusing the existing state-goal parse for clean/heat/cool forms and the existing object-token helper for trailing indices; skip lamp goals. From the request messages only: acquired = an earlier assistant take action containing the goal object token whose following observation head contains 'You pick up' AND the object token (noun-mismatch pickups such as goal 'soapbottle' vs observation 'soapbar' do NOT count as acquired); no-effect = a take/put/clean/heat/cool/use action within the last 4 whose observation head lacks the matching success phrase ('You pick up'/'You put'/'You clean'/'You heat'/'You cool'/'You turn'); offered-unvisited = 'go to <loc>'/'open <loc>' lines in AVAILABLE ACTIONS blocks of tool/user messages minus actions already chosen. Trigger: goal parsed AND object never acquired AND (one action chosen >= 4 times among the last 12 OR a no-effect manipulation within the last 4) AND at least one offered unvisited/unopened action. On trigger append '\n\n' plus a deterministic ~350-char redirect naming the object, destination, and up to 3 unvisited/unopened offers, stating that only the goal object counts, closed containers hide their contents, and an action on an object not held has no effect. Non-put/unparsable/malformed goals or no stall return the original request unchanged; stdlib json/re only, no new calls, no cross-episode state, no task-specific facts.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Redirect adds ~80-100 tokens only on triggered stuck calls. Replay over the 50 recorded incumbent requests (1402 calls): fires on 14/18 failing episodes and 2/32 passing episodes (truthful restatement), zero exceptions, remaining 34 episodes byte-identical. Flipped episodes should drop from 50 turns / 220-500K tokens to ~20 turns / ~100K, so batch tokens expected to fall ~8-12% even with per-call overhead on remaining failures. Pass rate predicted 0.64 -> 0.70-0.76 (4-6 flips among the 14-stall failures; main residual risk is 0-4pt loss if the 2 truthfully-firing passing episodes deteriorate).

candidate.name: offered_action_guard
candidate.hypothesis: A stateless offered-action guard that fires only when the most recently chosen action is absent from its immediately preceding AVAILABLE ACTIONS list (the uncovered signature of 15/16 failures, 96 calls; only 43 calls, mostly truthful restatements, on 18/34 passing episodes) will unstick 4-6 of those failures by revealing that the environment silently ignored the choice or performed a different offered action and by stating how to make the intended action offered, lifting the pass rate above the 0.68 incumbent while episodes whose last chosen action was offered stay byte-identical to stuck_search_redirect.
candidate.changes: In agents/offered_action_guard.py (byte-for-byte copy of stuck_search_redirect.py plus ONE new stateless layer applied LAST in transform_request, after repetition -> state -> light -> search-redirect, inside the existing try/except; transform_response stays identity): add _with_offered_action_guard plus three small helpers and one module constant _ACTION_VERBS (go/open/close/take/put/clean/heat/cool/use/move/examine/look/inventory/toggle). Reusing the file's existing _extract_action, _normalize, _offered_before and _ACTIONS_MARKER: scan messages backward for the most recent assistant action that normalizes to non-empty and matches a verb as a whole leading word (the whole-word rule keeps the malformed-JSON fallback tool name 'take_action' from being treated as an action); then take the nearest preceding tool/user message containing AVAILABLE ACTIONS and its parsed normalized offer set. Fire iff the offer set is non-empty and the normalized action is not in it; return the request unchanged when the action is offered, when no offer block parses, when no recent verb action exists, when the last message content is not a string, or on any malformed input. On fire, append '\n\n' plus a deterministic ~651-680 char reminder quoting the action verbatim: it was not offered at that step so it did not take effect - the environment either repeated the same view or silently performed a different offered action; do not repeat it; choose the next action verbatim from the offered list; an action is offered only while possible (take = at the object with empty hands, put = object in hands, open = closed container at this location, go to = a different destination); if the intended action is not offered, first choose an offered action that enables it. Module docstring extended with the fifth layer; stdlib json/re only, no new imports or runtime calls, no cross-episode state, no task names/ids/instance facts.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Guard adds ~651-680 chars (~165 tokens) only on fired calls. Read-only replay over all 50 recorded incumbent episodes (1421 model calls): fires on 139 calls - 96 in 15/16 failing episodes and 43 in 18/34 passing episodes (there a truthful restatement of a wasted turn) - for about +23.4K tokens, roughly +0.3% of the 7.93M batch. Prediction: pass rate 0.68 -> 0.72-0.78, central ~0.74-0.76, mainly flips among 116, 503, 1916, 2821, 2855/2362; residual ceiling ~0.80 because episodes where the goal object is never observed (1402/1479/2140/714) and one lamp-hold case (2232) are not addressed. Flips convert 50-turn / ~344K-token failures into roughly 20-turn / ~120K-token episodes, so batch tokens are expected to fall ~8-12% despite the per-call overhead; main risk is 0-4 pt loss if a firing passing episode's trajectory is disrupted.
